rationale: B shows timely, varied reactions to inputs and sustained, self-initiated shifts. It approaches on TOUCH (t=8–11), follows CALL (t=20–23), orients to OFFER_FOOD (t=32–43), responds to PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44–53), startles and withdraws (t=68–71), then develops new foci without prompts (SEALED_GATE t=54–63; SHELTER t=66–67) and later initiates play (PLAY_BOW t=94–95), with renewed vocal engagement to PERSON_ALPHA (t=78–83). A reacts to TOUCH (t=8–11), OFFER_FOOD (t=32–35), and STARTLE (t=68–71) but ignores CALL (t=20) and PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44), and spends long spans with attention NONE (t=40–67, 72–95). This pattern gives B higher apparent autonomy, coherence, adaptability, and overall aliveness.
